thread:
alex: I opened a small TF change to add per-AZ NAT gateways for HA in prod. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234. Can someone skim? plan looks ok but want a second pair of eyes on route tables and cost tags.

maria: quick q — are we doing one NAT per AZ or a single central NAT with AZ failover? cost jump is non-trivial if we add 3 more NAT gateways. :thinking:

alex: proposal is one NAT per private subnet AZ (module network -> nat.tf). Advantages: no cross-AZ data transfer and simpler routing. Downside: 3x NAT cost + EIPs. I'm attaching the snippet I changed: ```resource "aws_eip" "nat" {
  count = var.public_az_count
  vpc = true
  tags = merge(var.common_tags, { Name = "${local.name}-nat-${count.index}" })
}
resource "aws_nat_gateway" "nat" {
  count = var.public_az_count
  allocation_id = aws_eip.nat[count.index].id
  subnet_id     = aws_subnet.public[count.index].id
  tags = var.common_tags
}```

jon: FWIW for S3 traffic we could use gateway endpoints (aws_s3_bucket_endpoint) and avoid NAT for that egress-heavy workload. Are the prod services mostly S3-bound?

alex: Not only S3, some external APIs too. We still need NAT. I will add S3 endpoint separately.

priya: two quick checks: 1) ensure route-table associations are per-private-subnet and reference the right nat.id index; 2) tf state locking with our backend - if we create EIPs + NATs in the same apply, we should be fine but expect a ~5-10min window. Example route change: ```resource "aws_route" "private_internet" {
  count = var.private_subnet_count
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.private[count.index].id
  destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  nat_gateway_id = aws_nat_gateway.nat[count.index].id
}```

maria: also add cost_center tag (cc:infra) so finance can attribute. And add a note in PR about expected monthly delta.

alex: good call, will add tags and cost estimate. One other thing — I saw flakiness in staging where a private subnet lost its association to the right RT after a module refactor. Should we add an explicit depends_on?

jon: if you're changing module outputs, depends_on can be a bandaid but try to fix the module outputs first. deps_on for route might look like `depends_on = [aws_nat_gateway.nat]` for the route resource to avoid transient 0.0.0.0/0 missing.

deploy-bot: terraform plan completed for branch alex/nat-ha (workspace=staging) — 7 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. (link: https://ci.internal/redwood/terraform/456) :white_check_mark:

priya: I can run a dry-run apply in staging after you push tags. Also will validate that PrivateLink endpoints (we have com.amazonaws.vpce.s3 in account) are untouched.

alex: pushed tags + added cost note in PR. PTAL. If no objections I'll schedule apply in staging tomorrow 09:00 PT.

maria: :eyes: I'll review this evening. If it's green, we should proceed.

jon: LGTM for routing details. One minor: prefer `for_each` over `count` for subnet-index safety in future refactors.

alex: noted, I can follow up with a small refactor to for_each later. Thanks all.

priya: Approved to run in staging after maria's review. I'll monitor NAT gw creation and make sure alarms are in place for allocation EIP failures.
